one_liner: Senior executive (SES) who leads GSA's real estate strategy for client agencies, shaping office space solutions and representing PBS to Congress, OMB and agency leaders.
fit_summary: This is a Senior Executive Service role that requires demonstrated senior leadership in federal real property acquisition (lease, purchase, construction) and executive-level management of people and budgets. Daniel's policy knowledge, relationship skills and IEM consulting background match the stakeholder-engagement side, but nothing on file shows senior executive leadership or real estate experience. It is very unlikely to pass the SES panel and OPM QRB review.
eligibility: Open to all U.S. citizens (public and SES hiring paths), so no federal status is needed.
Your two-page resume must clearly show all three Mandatory Technical Competencies, including senior leadership in acquiring real property by lease, purchase or construction for client agencies.
Your resume must also demonstrate all five Executive Core Qualifications. Separate narratives will not be reviewed.

The role requires a Top Secret clearance before appointment, though you do not need one to apply. It also requires a drug test, an OGE 278 financial disclosure, and OPM QRB certification of your executive qualifications.
keywords: acquisition by lease, purchase or construction
strategy: Be honest with yourself about level: apply only if your IEM role involved managing teams, budgets and government client programs at a senior level. Otherwise, target GS-11 to GS-13 program analyst, emergency management or GSA customer relationship roles.
If you do apply, write the two-page resume so every bullet maps to an MTC or ECQ. Use the posting's exact phrases and state team size, budget and client agencies concisely.
Present your IEM work as government client strategy, emphasizing how you understood agency objectives, operational constraints and budgets for disaster recovery or preparedness clients.
Highlight briefings and persuasion aimed at federal, state or congressional stakeholders to support the third MTC and the Rule of Law ECQ.
Attend the November 9, 2026 information session at 1:00 pm ET, preview the posted interview questions, and submit before November 12, 2026.
Use the session to network with PBS staff and ask about lower-graded Office of Client Strategy roles, which would fit you far better.
resume_bullets: Served as [title] at IEM, supporting [client agency] on [disaster recovery/preparedness program]; aligned solutions with the client's operational and budgetary constraints across a [$ amount] portfolio.
Briefed and persuaded [number/type of senior officials, e.g., state emergency directors, congressional staff] on [strategy/recommendation], resulting in [outcome].
Led a team of [number] staff to [deliverable], tracking performance measures and metrics that [result].
interview_questions: Describe a time you developed a tailored solution for a client agency under tight budget and operational constraints.
How have you defended a team's strategy before Congress, OMB or other senior decision makers?
Give an example of driving efficiency by cutting waste or streamlining a process.
Tell us about leading people through change and holding staff accountable.
watch_outs: The SES level and real property MTCs almost certainly exceed your documented experience, so the application carries a high risk of being found ineligible.
The application window is short (October 27 to November 12, 2026), and the resume cannot exceed two pages.
Appointment requires a Top Secret clearance, a public financial disclosure, and a one-year SES probationary period.
The location is listed as multiple and may not be in the DC area.
